newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Boutros-Ghali to visit Paris, Hamburg, Lubeck.
newsitem.headline: Boutros-Ghali to visit Paris, Hamburg, Lubeck.

text.p: Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali will confer with French President Jacques Chirac and Foreign Minister Herve de Charette in Paris Wednesday on his way to Hamburg for the inauguration of the U.N. Law of the Sea tribunal, a U.N. source said on Monday.

His talks with the French leaders are expected to focus on African problems and a U.N. plan for limited Iraqi oil sales to finance the purchase of food and other humanitarian supplies, the source said.

The plan was agreed by the United Nations and Iraq in May but implementation has been delayed because fighting among Kurdish factions in northern Iraq has prevented the deployment of U.N. monitors on the ground.
Boutros-Ghali will fly to Hamburg late Wednesday for meetings the following day with the 21 judges of the tribunal that will rule on maritime disputes under the U.N. Law of the Sea convention.
The judges were elected at an August 1 meeting in New York of countries that are parties to the convention.
The secretary-general will also travel on Thursday to Lubeck to meet German Vice-Chancellor and Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel. On Friday he inaugurates the Law of the Sea tribunal in Hamburg.

On his way back to New York, Boutros-Ghali will stop over in Paris again to attend celebrations Saturday organised by the U.N. Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation honouring the life and work of former Senegalese President and writer Leopold Senghor on his 90th birthday.
